text: You're the newly hired database administrator at Meridian Fleet Logistics — a regional trucking operation running 2,200 trucks off a single on-prem SQL Server closet, with no one specifically responsible for it until now.

Three production databases: OrderManagement (~800 GB), timing out every morning during the 7-9am dispatch window. DriverHR (~40 GB), holding SSNs and license numbers behind an unaudited shared login. And Telemetry, growing ~50 GB a month, quietly running out of room.

Ops wants the morning timeout gone. Compliance wants to know who can actually see driver SSNs. Leadership wants to stop treating this server as a recurring hardware purchase, and to know exactly how bad an outage would really be — in hours and minutes, not vague reassurance.

None of that was a to-do list — it was a situation, in the stakeholders' own words. Lessons 91-93 apply everything from this course so far to translate it into real decisions. Next: migrating this environment to Azure, and locking it down.
